label: Third original token (t=2), when the first two tokens come from a preferred set (first in {o,x,3,m} or second in {a,d,y,i})
explanation: Fires almost only at the third input step (t=2, 99.7% of activation mass). It is silent at t=0,1, on the delimiter, and nearly silent in the copy phase. It does not depend on the current input token. Whether it fires and how strongly depends on the first two tokens, and the two effects look roughly additive: first token o/x/3/m (lift 3-5x) and second token a/d/y/i (lift 2.5-7x). The strongest activations (1.0) are on x a _, where both tokens are favored. Other first/second pairs give weak activations. The predicate captures 97% of the mass but precision is only about 0.62, because one favored token alone often is not enough. The real rule is a graded score over the bigram, not a clean set.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: o, 3, x, m, i, v; least: y, n, s, b) and the second original token (most: a, d, y, i, g, t; least: j, u, n, k); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, L=3 & t=5, t=3.
